# Jubilees Chapter 32 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Bethel; Levi's priestly designation; the seven tablets

---

**32:1** That night at Bethel an angel of the LORD appeared to Jacob and said: "I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the standing stone and made a vow to me. Arise and depart from this land and return to the land of your birth."

**32:2** Jacob rose early, summoned his wives and children and all that was his, and they journeyed and came to Bethel.

**32:3** Jacob offered a burnt offering at Bethel on the altar he had built, and he tithed everything that had come with him.

**32:4** In those days Levi had a dream: the angels of the LORD descended and appointed him to be a priest and to serve before the LORD.

**32:5** Jacob awoke from his sleep and blessed the LORD.

**32:6** Jacob counted all that belonged to him, beginning from his eldest sons: Reuben first, Simeon second, Levi third, Judah fourth, Dan fifth, Naphtali sixth, Gad seventh, Asher eighth, Issachar ninth, Zebulun tenth, Joseph eleventh, Benjamin twelfth.

**32:7** He counted again, and the lot came to Levi, for ten was the number that fell. On the second counting, Levi came out as the tenth.

**32:8** Jacob arose in the night and consecrated Levi, put clean garments on him, and anointed him with the holy oil.

**32:9** That same night, at the gate of Bethel, Jacob counted out ten from all his cattle for the LORD and set them apart — these were the tithe.

**32:10** In the morning he called his son Levi and read to him all the ordinances appointed for the priests, and charged him to minister before the LORD and to do all things as he had commanded.

**32:11** The LORD appeared to Jacob again at Bethel and blessed him, saying: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob; Israel shall be your name."

**32:12** He said to him: "I am the LORD your God who created the heavens and the earth. I will multiply you and make you fruitful, and kings will come forth from you and rule over all mankind.

**32:13** I will give to your descendants all the land under heaven, and they will rule over all the nations as they desire; and afterward they will take possession of the whole earth."

**32:14** When he had finished speaking with him, he ascended. Jacob watched until he had gone up into heaven.

**32:15** In a night vision Jacob saw an angel descend from heaven with seven tablets in his hands. The angel gave them to Jacob, and Jacob read them and knew all that was written in them — everything that would befall him and his sons throughout all the ages.

**32:16** Jacob showed the tablets to his father Isaac that night at Bethel. His father read them and wept, saying: "All these things will truly come upon your seed in generations to come."

**32:17** Isaac rejoiced over Jacob because Jacob's seed would be established as great. He blessed his son that night and slept.

**32:18** Jacob went to Rachel, who had conceived and was with child. Jacob wrote all these things in a book.

**32:19** In those days the Canaanites — the inhabitants of the land — rose up against Jacob and his children.

**32:20** But they did not prevail, for the LORD had spread fear and dread of Jacob over all the surrounding nations and peoples, and had given him glory, so that no one harmed him.

**32:21** Jacob's father-in-law Laban died that year. Jacob's sons were twelve in number.

**32:22** Rachel bore a second son, and Jacob named him Benjamin — "son of the days," that is, son of his old age.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus following LOGOS. The designation of Levi as the priestly tithe through the counting of Jacob's sons (vv.6-7) is a brilliant narrative device unique to Jubilees. The seven tablets vision is treated straightforwardly in all three renderings with no significant divergence in content.*
